data.long_meaning: In Greek, Sosthenes means 'savior' or 'deliverer'. This name appears in the New Testament, belonging to a Corinthian Christian leader who, along with Crispus, was baptized by the apostle Paul. The name Sosthenes carries the meaning “Given name of a Corinthian Christian leader” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sosthenes usually hope their child will grow to embody given name of a corinthian christian leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: סוסתנס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סוסתנס נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'σώζω' (להציל) ו'σθένος' (כוח). הוא מתאר אדם ששומר על כוחו ועל עצמו, ומופיע בתנ"ך כבן-לווי של פאולוס.

in_greek.name: Σωσθένης
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σωσθένης προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'σώζω' (σωτήριος) και 'σθένος' (δύναμη). Στο Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Σωσθένης αναφέρεται ως συνεργάτης του Παύλου.

in_latin.name: Sosthenes
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sosthenes ex vocabulis Graecis 'σώζω' (salvare) et 'σθένος' (fortitudo) derivatur. In ecclesia primitiva, Sosthenes ut socius Pauli mentionem habet.

in_english.name: Sosthenes
in_english.meaning: safe, sound, and strong; a guardian of strength
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sosthenes originates from Greek 'σώζω' (to save) and 'σθένος' (strength). It appears in the New Testament as a companion of Paul, signifying a person who preserves and safeguards strength. Historically, Sosthenes holds significance in Christian tradition as a symbol of resilience and spiritual fortitude.

data.cultural_impact: Sosthenes is a name deeply rooted in Greek and biblical history. It carries a distinguished heritage, being the name of a Corinthian Christian leader mentioned in the New Testament of the Bible. This not only highlights the cultural richness and influence of ancient Greece, but also the enduring impact of Christianity through its preservation and adaptation of Greek names.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sosthenes holds profound spiritual significance as a symbol of salvation and deliverance. In the Bible, Sosthenes is a Corinthian Christian leader who, along with Crispus, was baptized by the apostle Paul. This signifies the transformative power of faith and the spiritual journey that brought these individuals to the point of seeking salvation. The name Sosthenes serves as a reminder of the saving grace that God extends to all people and the redemptive power of faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sosthenes, meaning "man of God," embodies the spiritual strength and commitment to divine guidance that Christians strive for. He represents the inner fortitude to stand firm in faith amidst trials and tribulations, drawing strength from the Holy Spirit.

biblical_reference.note: Sosthenes is mentioned as the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, Sosthenes is mentioned as being present when the Apostle Paul addressed the elders of the Church of Ephesus (Acts 20:4). No further information about him is given.

The name Sosthenes is also mentioned in connection with a letter bearing the name 'First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians', which is an early Christian writing from around 96 AD. The author refers to 'Sosthenes our brother' and 'a man of Achaia', suggesting that he was a Christian leader in the city of Corinth during that time.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Sosthenes continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
